# Limiter skip log prints an impossible ratio when the reserve is in use

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Problem

`SlidingWindowRateLimiter.check_and_increment()` logs the rejection ratio as
`len(window)/max_rpm`, but with the free-tier reserve
(`LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`) the per-caller cap can be lower than the number of
entries already in the window, producing log lines that look like a bug:

```
WARNING - Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: 10/7 requests in 60s window
WARNING - Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=munitoai-free limit=7 reserve=3 ...
```

The `10` is the count in the window (including slots taken by in-progress
sessions), the `7` is the cap applied to this new-session request. Operators and
log analyses read `10/7` as an arithmetic error.

## Desired change

Make the message self-describing, e.g.:

```
Rate limit exceeded for munitoai-free: window=10 cap=7 (reserve in use) requests in 60s window
```

Keep the emitted fields parseable (stable `key=value` tokens) so the
proxy-usage / budget-effectiveness analyses can extract `window=` and `cap=`
instead of inferring them from provider config.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The rejection log line names both the in-window count and the cap applied to
  the rejected request, with no value that can read as `count/cap` confusion.
- A unit test asserts the emitted message contains `window=`, `cap=` and the
  correct numbers for (a) a plain over-limit rejection and (b) a
  reserve-limited rejection (cap < window count).
- No behaviour change: only the message text (and any consumed parse) changes;
  full project test suite passes.
- Stale references quoting the old `N/M requests in Ns window` wording are
  updated to the new format (see Affected references).

## Implementation notes

- The limiter only knows the cap it was handed (`effective_limit`); it does not
  know *why* that cap is below the configured `rate_limit_rpm`. A
  `(reserve in use)` annotation therefore requires the caller
  (`proxy/provider_budget.py`) to pass context, and is optional — the required,
  parseable fields are `window=` and `cap=`.
- If extra context is passed, prefer a stable token over prose so the
  `key=value` convention used by the companion `Provider budget exhausted`
  line is preserved (e.g. `cap=7 reserve=3`, not `(reserve in use)`).
- Test-first: add the message assertions to `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py`
  (plain over-limit case and `cap < window` case) before changing the format
  string.

## Affected references

- `proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py` — the format string and `logger.warning` call.
- `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py` — unit tests asserting the message fields.
- `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py` — comment quoting the old
  `13/11 requests in 60s window` wording.
- `proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md` — same quoted wording.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/proxy/rate_limiter.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_rate_limiter.py`
- `proxy/docs/remote-fallback-timeout-budget.md`
data.title: Limiter skip log prints 10/7 when the reserve is in use

# Consolidate and document the provider fallback-chain configuration model

discovered-from:LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want **one** authoritative description of the provider
fallback model — every knob that shapes a chain, the layer it applies at
(provider entry / model / server), and the order those layers win in — so I can
answer "how do I control X for model Y?" without reading `provider.py`, and so
new controls (e.g. per-model budget knobs, `LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV`) slot into a
documented contract instead of inventing a new shape.

Low priority: documentation/consolidation only, no behaviour change.

## Current state (fragmented)

Fallback behaviour is described in five places that have drifted apart:
`proxy/config.yaml` header comments, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`,
`proxy/docs/routing.md` and inline code comments in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` /
`provider_budget.py`. The knobs themselves are spread across three layers with
no single statement of precedence:

| Layer | Examples | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Provider entry | `rate_limit_rpm`, `available_times`, `endpoint`, `api_key_env`, `forward_session_headers`, `api`, `system_prompt`, `budget` (proposed) | per-entry, order defines chain position |
| Model (`models.<name>`) | `providers` list order, `aliases`, `system_prompt`, `budget` (proposed) | one model key → one chain, shared by all aliases |
| Server (`server.*`) | `provider_cooldown_seconds`, `sibling_fallback_*`, `chain_hold_*`, `upstream_*`, `provider_rate_limit_*`, `provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`, `max_retry_after_seconds` | global; some are inherited-only across mode overlays |
| Mode overlay | `config-fast.yaml`, `config-cheap.yaml` | lists replace wholesale; other values replace; only diffs declared |
| Runtime | cooldowns, usage-limit quarantine, stall circuit breaker, affinity records, budget windows | in-memory + `proxy/provider-state.json` |

Cross-cutting semantics that are easy to get wrong and belong in one place:
failure-domain grouping (shared endpoint+model), per-account vs per-endpoint
exclusion, time windows (`available_times`), the free-tier budget gate
(`LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL`, `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20`) including the reserve and
affinity, chain-hold retry cycles, sibling-fallback circuit breaker,
mode grandfathering, and which of these reset on proxy restart (in-memory vs
persisted).

## Desired change

1. A single reference document (e.g. `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md`)
   covering: chain resolution order, every knob with its layer + default +
   precedence, the failure/cooldown/quarantine taxonomies, quota/budget gating,
   mode overlays and grandfathering, and what is persisted vs in-memory.
2. `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` link to it instead of duplicating
   the detail (keep short, task-focused sections there).
3. A short "inconsistencies / gaps" section recording anything found while
   writing it (knobs only available globally, provider lists duplicated in the
   fast overlay, budget gating only on one entry, etc.) — recorded as
   `discovered-from` work items rather than fixed here.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md` exists and states, for every
   fallback-related knob: name, layer, default, precedence, and the behaviour it
   controls — verified against the code paths that read it (no invented values).
2. A precedence table covers entry > model (where applicable) > server >
   built-in default, including the mode-overlay merge rule (lists replace,
   scalars replace, dicts merge) and the `BASE_ONLY_SERVER_KEYS` inheritance
   contract.
3. The persistence section distinguishes state that survives a restart
   (`provider-state.json`, grandfathered bindings) from in-memory state
   (cooldowns, stall breaker, affinity, budget windows).
4. `proxy/README.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` link to the new document and no
   longer contradict it.
5. Every inconsistency found is either fixed by a linked `discovered-from` item
   or explicitly recorded as accepted.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments where a pointer to the new document replaces duplicated prose.
7. Full project test suite passes (documentation-only change must not perturb
   behaviour).

## Constraints

- Documentation/analysis only: no behaviour, config-value or code-path changes in
  this item.
- Do not duplicate the new budget-gate material — reference
  `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` / `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` and the per-model controls item
  (`LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV`) rather than restating their designs.
- UK English, Markdown, no secrets (reference API keys by env-var name only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/docs/provider-fallback-model.md` — new reference document.
- `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md` — link + trim
  duplicated material.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — header comments point at the document.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — verify claims;
  replace duplicated comments with pointers only where clearly redundant.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV` — per-model budget knobs (the contract this document
  should describe once it lands).
- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL`, `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` — the free-tier budget gate,
  reserve and wait cap.
- `LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4` — whether `rate_limit_rpm` should be raised.
- `LP-0MVDNP36J006430L` — header-derived budgeting.
- `LP-0MVDQKF4F008LGS6` — free tier restricted to cheap mode.
data.title: Consolidate and document the provider fallback-chain configuration model

## Goal

As the proxy operator I want the client-side bridge to log one line per
captured compaction signal and one line per reshape attempt, so that a
loaded-but-idle extension (bridge installed, no signal ever arrives) is
distinguishable from a broken one (signal arrived, bridge did nothing) —
satisfying AC4's client half and making the parent's pass criterion D
(ordering evidence) observable.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8. Unconditional — required whether or not Phase B
passes.

## Cross-repo constraint (read first)

This work lands in the **SorraAgents** repository, not this one:

- code: `~/projects/SorraAgents/pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/`
  (`index.ts` adapter + `compaction-bridge.js` pure core),
- tests: `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`,
- loaded via the symlink `~/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-compaction-bridge` →
  that directory (verified present 2026-10-31), so no reinstall is needed
  beyond `/reload` inside pi.

The commit hash in SorraAgents must be recorded on this child and on the
parent, so the client half of AC4 is traceable from the LP item. Do not copy
the bridge into this repository.

## Current state (verified during planning)

- `compaction-bridge.js` has no logging at all: `handleResponse` returns a
  boolean, `reshape` returns a list or `null`. Neither reports why.
- `index.ts` wires `after_provider_response` and `context` and silently
  returns on a stale ctx / missing signal.
- There is no `ctx.ui` in print or JSON mode (`docs/extensions.md`), so
  `ctx.ui.notify` cannot be the logging channel — headless T2 would lose it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: One line per **captured** signal, emitted from the pure core:
  `compaction-bridge signal captured session=<id8> turns_summarized=<n>
  recent_turns_kept=<k> marker_chars=<len>`.
- AC2: One line per **reshape attempt**:
  - applied: `compaction-bridge reshaped <X>-><Y> messages session=<id8>`
    with `Y < X`,
  - not applicable: `compaction-bridge no signal — passthrough session=<id8>`
    (state absent) — the "loaded but idle" line, and
  - anomalous signal (fewer turns than `turnsSummarized`):
    `compaction-bridge reshape refused reason=insufficient_turns session=<id8>`.
- AC3: Exactly one line per event: `handleResponse` logs once whether or not a
  signal was parsed (no-signal case logs at most once per response, and is
  rate-limited to one line per session per turn so an idle session does not
  spam), and `reshape` logs once per `context` event.
- AC4: Works in every pi mode (interactive, RPC, JSON, print): no `ctx.ui`
  dependency. Lines go to **stderr** and, when
  `PROXY_COMPACTION_BRIDGE_LOG` is set, are appended to that file, one line
  each. The default channel and the optional file path are documented in the
  extension README.
- AC5: No marker text, no message content and no summary body in any line —
  session id (truncated to 8), counts and lengths only.
- AC6: Logging never changes behaviour and never throws: the logger is
  injected into `createCompactionBridge({ log })` with a no-op default, so the
  pure module stays dependency-free and a hostile/throwing logger leaves
  parse/reshape results identical.
- AC7: `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs` extended to assert: the AC1 line
  and its fields; the AC2 applied / passthrough / refused lines; the AC3
  one-line-per-event rule including the idle no-spam case; the AC5 no-body
  guarantee (assert the marker string does not appear in any captured line);
  and AC6 (identical `parseCompactionSignal` / `reshapeContext` results with a
  no-op logger vs a throwing logger). All pre-existing bridge tests stay green
  unmodified.
- AC8: README documents the exact log lines, the `PROXY_COMPACTION_BRIDGE_LOG`
  variable, and the grep recipe used by T2's criterion D.
- (Parent AC4) the proxy logs one INFO per header emission (session, `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`, marker length) and the bridge logs one line per signal capture and one per reshape. A reader of the logs can tell "no signal emitted" from "signal emitted, bridge ignored it".

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a `log` option to `createCompactionBridge({ log } = {})` defaulting to a
  no-op; the default writer lives in `index.ts` (adapter layer), keeping
  `compaction-bridge.js` free of `fs`/`process` imports except behind an
  injected function.
- Emit from inside `handleResponse` / `reshape` where the decision is already
  made — no re-parsing, no extra state.
- Idle rate-limiting is one `Set` of session ids already logged for
  passthrough, cleared when a signal is captured for that session (keeps the
  module dependency-free and the logic pure).
- Keep the existing public surface (`handleResponse` boolean, `reshape` list or
  null) unchanged so `index.ts` and the tests need no behavioural edits.
- Run `node --test` for the extension's unit test only via the test skill
  (`/skill:test` scope) — not ad-hoc.

## Deliverables

- `compaction-bridge.js` telemetry + injected logger.
- `index.ts` default logger wiring (stderr + optional file).
- `README.md` log-line documentation.
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs` extended coverage.
- SorraAgents commit hash recorded on this item.

**Key Files:**

- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/README.md`
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`

## Dependencies

None. Required by the T2 execution child (pass criterion D reads these lines).
data.title: Bridge telemetry: signal-captured and reshape log lines (SorraAgents)

# Router-mode /slots observability regression: per-slot state frozen for 8h+, blocking dispatch

**Related:** LP-0MW1VDZIX0011D8M (payload truth), LP-0MW1VDZTC00034S7 (lifecycle/log path).

**Priority:** critical - this is actively preventing work from being scheduled right now.
**Type:** bug · **Risk:** High · **Effort:** M

## Impact

`GET /llama/local/status` has published `slots_stale=true` continuously since
**2026-11-04 00:26:18** (8h17m at time of filing, still true). The downtime
dispatcher fails closed on `slots_stale` by contract
(WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW), so **no new work has been scheduled** since 00:26:13.
The proxy has no bounded staleness ceiling, no escalation and no recovery path,
so this degrades silently and indefinitely.

## Evidence (all reproduced on the live host, 2026-11-04)

**1. Router mode means `/slots` is queried wrong.** The local model now runs as
a llama-server router with autoloaded children:

```text
$ curl -s :8080/props
{"role":"router","models_autoload":true,"model_path":"none","total_slots":null}

$ curl -s :8080/slots
400 {"error":{"code":400,"message":"model name is missing from the request","type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

Router mode requires a `model` parameter; the proxy sends none, so every poll
fails with `reason="unknown"`.

**2. Child-port discovery is dead, and has been since before the outage.**

```text
llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"} 26331
llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_created{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"} 1.7937235741837883e+09  # 2026-11-03 16:32:54
llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="timeout"}  6290
llama_slots_query_failures_created{reason="timeout"}  1.7937235779758415e+09  # 2026-11-03 16:32:57
llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="unknown"}  9476
llama_slots_query_failures_created{reason="unknown"}  1.7937519781348174e+09  # 2026-11-04 00:26:18
```

Note the two distinct dates: child-port discovery broke at the **16:32 restart**
and dispatch still worked for ~7h45m afterwards (heavy traffic until 00:15). The
`/slots` 400s start at **00:26:18**, which is when the snapshot froze. The
regression is therefore the `/slots` model-parameter path, not router mode per
se - do not stop at "router mode is unsupported".

**3. The frozen snapshot is served forever.** Last successful `/slots` read:

```text
$ tail -3 /var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.1.log   # mtime 2026-11-04 00:26:07.826
[44809] srv  log_server_r: done request: GET /slots 127.0.0.1 200
[44809] srv  log_server_r: done request: GET /slots 127.0.0.1 200
start-llama.sh: line 273: 191448 Killed "${LLAMA_CMD[@]}"
```

Current payload (08:42):

```text
slots_stale=true slots_detail_stale=true
slots_snapshot_source=snapshot
slots_snapshot_age_seconds=29825.67        # 8h17m, unbounded
available_slots=2 capacity_hint=idle local_abandoned_slots=2 local_in_flight_requests=0
```

The snapshot age is published but never enforced.

**4. Consequences downstream.** `slot_save` fails against the phantom slots:

```text
2026-11-04 04:36:49,287 - WARNING - slot_save failed slot=0 status=501
  body={"error":{"code":501,"message":"This server does not support slots action. Start it with `--slot-save-path`"}}
```

and the proxy continues to evict leases against slot ids it cannot observe.

## Change

1. **Query `/slots` correctly in router mode** - pass the model parameter the
   router requires (e.g. `GET /slots?model=<id>`) instead of the unparameterised
   path.
2. **Restore child-port discovery for autoloaded children** (children bind
   `--port 0`), or make the router-port-with-model query the supported path and
   delete the dead fallback.
3. **Bound the snapshot.** A snapshot older than a configurable ceiling
   (proposed `local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds`, default a small multiple of
   the dispatch decision cadence) must never be presented as a live slot list -
   see LP-0MW1VDZIX0011D8M "`available_slots` contradicts its own `slots[]`" for
   the payload-truth half.
4. **Give `slots_stale` a machine-readable reason** (`router_model_missing`,
   `child_port_undiscovered`, `query_timeout`, `query_error`,
   `snapshot_too_old`) so an operator can distinguish the failure modes without
   reading counter names.
5. **Surface it on `/health`** - a stale slot surface is a serving deficiency and
   must appear in the health payload, not only in `/metrics` counters that
   nobody scrapes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Against a live router-mode llama-server (`role: router`,
      `models_autoload: true`), the proxy obtains per-slot detail: a test
      fixture where `/slots` without `model` returns 400 and with `model`
      returns slot detail asserts the proxy gets the detail and does not fall
      back to a snapshot.
- [ ] `slots_snapshot_age_seconds` is bounded: past the configured ceiling the
      proxy publishes an explicit stale reason and never reports availability
      from the stale list.
- [ ] `slots_stale` carries an enumerated, machine-readable reason; every value
      in the list is emitted by a covered code path.
- [ ] A stale slot surface is reported in `/health` (a field plus a non-OK
      status), so the condition is visible without reading `/metrics`.
- [ ] No unbounded staleness: a test advances the clock past the ceiling and
      asserts the payload stops claiming availability (this is the actual
      defect - an 8-hour freeze must be impossible).
- [ ] Live verification recorded: after the fix and a proxy restart,
      `slots_stale=false`, `slots_snapshot_age_seconds` below the ceiling, and a
      real `GET /slots?model=…` 200 in `llama-server`'s log.
- [ ] Restart of the local model is no longer required to clear the condition
      (recovery is automatic once `/slots` answers).
- [ ] Full test suite green via the test skill.
data.title: Router-mode /slots observability regression: per-slot state frozen 8h+, blocking dispatch

# Regression fence: router-mode `/slots` model param must yield live detail

Parent: LP-0MW1VDWY0007EMH7 (router-mode `/slots` observability regression).
Slice 1 of 5 — **test-first**, before any production change.

## Why this is first

The model-parameter path (`?model=`) and child-port discovery were both
implemented after the 2026-11-04 incident (LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW,
LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF, LP-0MVWBXEAI008YZ7B), but there is **no single
end-to-end fixture** proving the contract the incident broke: a router-mode
server that answers `400` to model-less `/slots` and slot detail to
`/slots?model=<id>`. The existing tests fence pieces
(`test_slots_model_param_guard.py` scans call sites;
`test_slots_model_id_resolution.py` resolves ids;
`test_child_port_discovery_rotation.py` rotates ports) but nothing asserts
the composed behaviour: *the proxy obtains detail and does not fall back to
a snapshot.*

This item is the tracer bullet: it pins the AC1 contract with a test that
fails loudly if `?model=` is ever dropped again, and it proves the incident
root cause is closed before slices 2-4 add new behaviour on top.

## Scope

**New file** `proxy/tests/test_slots_router_mode_detail.py`:

1. A fake llama-server router fixture where `GET /slots` (no `model`) returns
   `400 {"error":{"code":400,"message":"model name is missing from the request"}}`
   and `GET /slots?model=<id>` returns a 2-slot detail list.
2. Assert `GET /llama/local/status` against that fixture returns the live
   detail: `slots` has 2 entries with the fixture's `slot_id`s,
   `slots_detail_stale` is `false`, `slot_counts_stale` is `false`, and
   `slots_snapshot_source` is **not** `"snapshot"`.
3. Assert a *second* poll still shows the same slot identities (no fossil
   swap-in) and that the upstream call count is non-zero.
4. Assert the router-mode child-port preference: when a discoverable child
   port exists, the `/slots` request goes to the child port, and the
   `no_child_port_router_mode` fallback counter does not increment.
5. Assert the negative control: with `/slots?model=` also broken (400), the
   payload reports `slots_detail_stale: true` and a snapshot source — i.e.
   the test genuinely distinguishes the two regimes and is not vacuous.

Reuse `proxy/tests/gpu_fixtures.py` and the status-handler test harness used
by `proxy/tests/test_slots_detail_cache_fallback.py`; do not build a second
harness.

If any assertion fails against current `dev`, the fix belongs in this item —
the fence must be green, not marked `xfail`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Against a router-mode llama-server fixture (`role: router`,
      `models_autoload: true`) where `/slots` without `model` returns 400 and
      with `model` returns slot detail, the proxy obtains per-slot detail and
      does not fall back to a snapshot.
- [ ] The detail assertion checks the fixture's `slot_id`s with
      `slots_detail_stale=false` and `slots_snapshot_source != "snapshot"`.
- [ ] A negative-control assertion proves the test distinguishes a working
      `?model=` path from a failing one (the failing control yields
      `slots_detail_stale=true`).
- [ ] The test asserts the child-port preference and that the
      `no_child_port_router_mode` fallback is not taken when a child port is
      discoverable.
- [ ] No production behaviour is changed by this slice (test-only); the
      changed-scope gate passes.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_slots_router_mode_detail.py` (new)
- `proxy/tests/gpu_fixtures.py` (reuse fixtures)
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_detail_cache_fallback.py` (reuse harness patterns)
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` (read-only reference: `_query_slots`,
  `_query_slots_detail`)
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` (read-only reference: `get_llama_local_status`)

## Dependencies

None. Blocks slices 2-5.

## Notes

- Do not restate or duplicate `test_slots_model_param_guard.py`'s static
  call-site scan; this item is about composed runtime behaviour.
- If the fixture needs a real port, bind `:0` and use the existing
  `httpx` mock-client injection points (`_client=` / `base_url=`) rather than
  opening sockets — the suite must stay offline and fast.

# Enumerated `slots_stale_reason` on the local status payload

Parent: LP-0MW1VDWY0007EMH7. Slice 2 of 5. Depends on slice 1
(LP-0MW1VDWY0007EMH7's first child — router-mode detail fence).

## Problem

`/llama/local/status` publishes `slots_stale` / `slots_detail_stale` as bare
booleans. During the 2026-11-04 incident an operator could only learn *why*
by reading counter names in `/metrics`
(`llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`,
`llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="timeout"}`, `…{reason="unknown"}`).
The status payload itself gave no machine-readable cause, so the dispatcher
and any dashboard could only fail closed blindly.

## Change

Introduce a canonical, enumerated staleness-reason vocabulary and publish it
as `slots_stale_reason` on `/llama/local/status`:

| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `router_model_missing` | the resolved `/slots` query carried no usable model id (resolution fell through to a last resort that the server rejected) |
| `child_port_undiscovered` | router mode, no child port discoverable — the query went to the router port |
| `query_timeout` | the `/slots` fetch timed out |
| `query_error` | any other fetch failure (HTTP non-200, connection error, malformed payload) |
| `snapshot_too_old` | the served snapshot is older than the configured ceiling (added in slice 3) |

`slots_stale_reason` is `None` when the payload is fresh. Precedence is
documented and tested: detail-phase failure dominates counts-phase failure
(detail is what capacity consumes), and `snapshot_too_old` dominates every
transport-level reason once the ceiling is exceeded.

Implementation sketch:

- A module-level frozen vocabulary constant (e.g.
  `SLOTS_STALE_REASONS` in `proxy/observability.py`) that the tests can
  iterate for exhaustiveness — no bare string literals at call sites.
- An in-process last-reason recorder fed from the existing `status_out`
  dict (`_query_slots`) and the resolver outcome
  (`_resolve_local_slots_target`), plus the detail-fetch failure path.
  Fail-open: a recorder fault must never break the status endpoint.
- Classification helpers mapping the existing metric labels
  (`timeout`, `http_<code>`, `connection_error`, `invalid_payload`,
  `unknown`) onto the new vocabulary — the metric labels stay unchanged so
  `monitoring/slots_query_alerts.yaml` keeps working.

`status_schema_version` is bumped to `6` (additive fields).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `/llama/local/status` publishes `slots_stale_reason`, `None` when
      `slots_stale` is false.
- [ ] `slots_stale` carries an enumerated, machine-readable reason; every
      value in the list is emitted by a covered code path (the vocabulary is a
      single importable constant and a test iterates it).
- [ ] `query_timeout` is emitted when the `/slots` fetch raises a timeout.
- [ ] `query_error` is emitted for a non-200 HTTP response, a connection
      error and a malformed payload (parametrised test).
- [ ] `router_model_missing` is emitted when model-id resolution reaches its
      last resort and the server rejects the query.
- [ ] `child_port_undiscovered` is emitted when router mode is active and no
      child port is discoverable (the `no_child_port_router_mode` fallback
      path).
- [ ] Documented precedence is asserted: detail-phase failure wins over
      counts-phase failure; a recorder exception degrades to `None` without
      breaking the payload.
- [ ] `status_schema_version` is `6` and the existing metric label
      vocabulary is unchanged (alert rules still match).
- [ ] Existing `/llama/local/status` tests stay green.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` (`_query_slots` / `_query_slots_detail`
  reason capture, vocabulary constant, recorder)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` (`_resolve_local_slots_target` outcome)
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` (`get_llama_local_status` payload +
  `status_schema_version`)
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_stale_reason.py` (new)
- `monitoring/slots_query_alerts.yaml` (read-only: labels must not change)

## Out of scope

- The age ceiling itself (`snapshot_too_old` is *declared* here, *enforced*
  in slice 3).
- `/health` surfacing (slice 4).
- The `available_slots` vs `slots[]` contradiction — that is
  LP-0MW1VDZIX0011D8M.

data.description:
# Bound the slot snapshot: `local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds` ceiling

Parent: LP-0MW1VDWY0007EMH7. Slice 3 of 5. Depends on slice 2
(`slots_stale_reason` vocabulary).

## Problem — this is the actual defect

`slots_snapshot_age_seconds` was published (**29825.67 s ≈ 8 h 17 m**) but
never enforced: `slots_detail_stale=true` plus `slots_snapshot_source=snapshot`
served a frozen per-slot list indefinitely. The counts cache *is* bounded
(`SLOT_COUNTS_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS`, default 1 h, via
`last_known_slot_counts()`), but the **per-slot detail cache**
(`observability._last_slot_details_cache` / `_last_slot_details_at`) has no
bound at all — it is served until a fresh query succeeds, which never
happened. `available_slots=2 capacity_hint=idle` was therefore asserted from
an 8-hour-old snapshot, and the dispatcher fails closed on `slots_stale`,
stopping all scheduling.

## Change

1. **New knob**, `local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds`, resolved
   config-first (`server.local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds`) with an env
   fallback (`LOCAL_SLOTS_MAX_SNAPSHOT_AGE_SECONDS`), matching how
   `SLOT_COUNTS_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS` is already read. Default: a small
   multiple of the `/llama/local/status` poll cadence — derive and document
   it (e.g. `max(120, 10 × poll interval)`, ~300 s) rather than hard-coding an
   arbitrary hour. Invalid/unparseable values fall back to the default and log
   once (never raise).
2. **Enforce it**: past the ceiling the proxy stops serving the stale detail
   cache — `slots` becomes an empty array and the payload reports
   `slots_detail_stale=true` with `slots_stale_reason="snapshot_too_old"`.
3. **Never claim availability from a too-old list**: `capacity_hint` must not
   report `idle`/`available` derived from detail older than the ceiling, and
   `available_slots` must not be resurrected from a stale cache by the detail
   path. Recovery is automatic: the next successful `/slots` poll restores
   fresh detail with no restart (AC7 of the parent).
4. Document the knob alongside `SLOT_COUNTS_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS` in the
   status-handler docstring and the operator docs (`docs/llama-router.md` or a
   new `docs/local-slots-observability.md` — whichever the implementer finds
   already hosts slot-status knob docs).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds` is read config-first with an env
      fallback; a test covers config value, env value, absent (documented
      default) and an unparseable value (falls back to default, logs, does not
      raise).
- [ ] No unbounded staleness: a test advances the clock past the ceiling and
      asserts the payload stops claiming availability (this is the actual
      defect — an 8-hour freeze must be impossible). Concretely: with a frozen
      detail cache and a monotonic clock advanced past the ceiling, `slots` is
      empty, `capacity_hint` does not claim live idle capacity,
      `slots_detail_stale=true`, and
      `slots_stale_reason="snapshot_too_old"`.
- [ ] `slots_snapshot_age_seconds` is bounded: past the configured ceiling the
      proxy publishes an explicit stale reason and never reports availability
      from the stale list.
- [ ] Below the ceiling the existing graceful-degradation behaviour is
      unchanged: the stale snapshot is still served with
      `slots_snapshot_source="snapshot"` and its true age.
- [ ] `slots_snapshot_age_seconds` is still published and equals the true
      distance from the snapshot's own fetch stamp (never re-stamped).
- [ ] Restart of the local model is no longer required to clear the condition
      (recovery is automatic once `/slots` answers): after the cache ages past
      the ceiling, a subsequent successful `/slots?model=…` poll returns a
      fresh payload with `slots_stale=false` and `slots_stale_reason=null`, with
      no restart or process-state reset.
- [ ] The default ceiling is derived from the poll cadence in code (not a
      magic literal) and is asserted by a test.
- [ ] Knob documented (docstring + operator doc) and existing
      `test_slots_detail_cache_fallback.py` expectations are reconciled rather
      than deleted.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` (`get_llama_local_status`: detail fallback,
  `capacity_hint`, `available_slots`, ceiling resolution)
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` (`_last_slot_details_cache` /
  `_last_slot_details_at` accessors, ceiling helper beside
  `_slots_counts_stale_after_seconds`)
- `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` (defaults, if the knob is declared there)
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_snapshot_ceiling.py` (new)
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_detail_cache_fallback.py` (reconcile)
- `docs/llama-router.md` (or new `docs/local-slots-observability.md`)

## Out of scope

- `/health` surfacing (slice 4).
- The `available_slots` vs `slots[]` contradiction when the data is *fresh*
  (LP-0MW1VDZIX0011D8M).
- Restarting or reconfiguring the live llama-server
  (LP-0MW1VDZTC00034S7).

# Surface slot staleness on `/health`

Parent: LP-0MW1VDWY0007EMH7. Slice 4 of 5. Depends on slice 3 (age ceiling).

## Problem

An 8-hour degraded slot surface was invisible to health consumers. `/health`
reports `status`, `ready`, `llama_server_running`, `backend_reachable`,
`llama_log_age_seconds`, … but nothing about the slot surface, so
`slot_sweep_preflight.py`, machine-hygiene, dashboards and the operator all
saw `healthy` while the dispatcher was starved by `slots_stale=true`. The
condition only existed in `/metrics` counters nobody scrapes.

## Change

Add these **additive** fields to `GET /health`:

- `slots_surface_status`: `"ok"` | `"stale"` | `"unknown"` — the non-OK
  marker the parent AC asks for.
- `slots_stale`: bool (mirrors the status payload).
- `slots_stale_reason`: the enumerated reason from slice 2, else `null`.
- `slots_snapshot_age_seconds`: float | null.
- `slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds`: the effective ceiling, so a consumer can
  judge severity without knowing the config.

**`ready` semantics are deliberately unchanged.** `ready` gates request
admission; a stale slot *surface* does not make the proxy unable to serve
requests, and flipping `ready` would fail-closed every consumer that today
reads `ready` for liveness (the 2026-11-02 orphan-backend regression
LP-0MVZT9L3N001XABB AC2 is the cautionary precedent). The non-OK signal is
`slots_surface_status != "ok"`. This decision must be stated in the
docstring so a future reader does not "fix" it into `ready`.

The fields must be computed from the **same** shared staleness evaluation the
status payload uses (single source of truth) — do not duplicate the ceiling
arithmetic in the health handler.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A stale slot surface is reported in `/health` (a field plus a non-OK
      status), so the condition is visible without reading `/metrics` — via
      `slots_surface_status`, `slots_stale`, `slots_stale_reason`,
      `slots_snapshot_age_seconds` and `slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds`.
- [ ] When the slot surface is fresh, `slots_surface_status == "ok"` and
      `slots_stale` is false.
- [ ] When detail staleness is reported (either a transient snapshot *or* the
      `snapshot_too_old` ceiling), `slots_surface_status == "stale"` and
      `slots_stale_reason` matches the status payload's value exactly — one
      test asserts the `/health` and `/llama/local/status` fields agree for
      each reason.
- [ ] When the slot state cannot be determined (llama-server down / no model
      loaded), `slots_surface_status == "unknown"` rather than `"stale"`, so
      a normal idle window is not reported as a defect.
- [ ] `ready` and top-level `status` are provably **unchanged** by slot
      staleness — a test asserts `ready` stays true on a stale slot surface
      with a healthy backend, and the docstring states the rationale.
- [ ] A slot-staleness fault never raises: an exception in the shared
      evaluator yields `slots_surface_status="unknown"` and a well-formed
      payload.
- [ ] Existing `/health` tests (`test_health_probe_router_slots.py` and
      related) stay green.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` (`health_check`, plus the shared staleness
  helper extracted/reused in slice 3)
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` (staleness evaluation + reason)
- `proxy/tests/test_health_slots_surface.py` (new)
- `proxy/tests/test_health_probe_router_slots.py` (regression)
- `scripts/slot_sweep_preflight.py` (read-only: a consumer that may now read
  the new field — wire only if a test covers it)

## Out of scope

- Changing admission or routing behaviour (no consumer is required to act on
  the new fields in this slice).
- Prometheus alert-rule changes.
data.title: Surface slot staleness on /health

# Docs, verify script and recorded live evidence

Parent: LP-0MW1VDWY0007EMH7. Slice 5 of 5. Depends on slice 4 (`/health`
surfacing).

## Problem

The parent item's ACs require (a) operator documentation of the new
staleness contract and (b) *recorded live verification* after a proxy
restart: `slots_stale=false`, `slots_snapshot_age_seconds` below the ceiling,
and a real `GET /slots?model=…` `200` in llama-server's log. Without a
deterministic script, that evidence is an ad-hoc shell session nobody can
reproduce or audit.

## Change

1. **`docs/local-slots-observability.md`** (new, or extend
   `docs/llama-router.md` if it already covers `/slots` honestly):
   - the staleness contract: `slots_stale`, `slots_detail_stale`,
     `slots_snapshot_source`, `slots_snapshot_age_seconds`;
   - the full `slots_stale_reason` vocabulary with the operator action for
     each value;
   - the `local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds` knob, its default derivation
     and env fallback;
   - the `/health` fields and the explicit note that `ready` is unchanged;
   - the recovery expectation: **no restart is required** — the surface
     clears on the next successful `/slots?model=…` poll, and what to do if it
     does not.
2. **`scripts/verify_slots_observability.py`** — a deterministic verifier that
   queries a running proxy and prints a PASS/FAIL evidence block:
   - `/props` role (router or not), `/llama/local/status` (`slots_stale`,
     reason, source, age, ceiling), `/health` fields;
   - the newest `GET /slots` line from the llama-server log with its status
     code and whether the request carried `?model=`;
   - exit code `0` only when `slots_stale=false`, age < ceiling and a
     `200` model-bearing `/slots` line is present.
   Offline-unit-testable: inject the HTTP fetcher and log reader.
3. **Record the live run** as a comment on the parent work item: verifier
   output, host timestamp, proxy restart confirmation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/local-slots-observability.md` documents the staleness contract,
      the complete `slots_stale_reason` vocabulary with operator actions, the
      ceiling knob and default, the `/health` fields, and the
      no-restart-required recovery path.
- [ ] The doc's reason list is asserted to match the code's vocabulary
      constant exactly (doc/code drift test, mirroring
      `test_slots_model_resolution_docs.py`).
- [ ] `scripts/verify_slots_observability.py` exists and, with injected
      fetcher/log-reader fixtures, returns exit `0` for a healthy surface and
      non-zero for: `slots_stale=true`, age ≥ ceiling, and a missing
      model-bearing `200` `/slots` log line (three named failing cases).
- [ ] The script never mutates state (read-only HTTP GETs and log reads) and
      its `--help` documents how to obtain the evidence block.
- [ ] Live verification recorded: after the fix and a proxy restart,
      `slots_stale=false`, `slots_snapshot_age_seconds` below the ceiling, and
      a real `GET /slots?model=…` `200` in `llama-server`'s log — recorded as a
      parent-work-item comment with the verifier output and host timestamp.
- [ ] The live run confirms restart of the local model is no longer required
      to clear the condition (recovery is automatic once `/slots` answers).
- [ ] Full test suite green via the test skill.

## Key Files

- `docs/local-slots-observability.md` (new)
- `docs/llama-router.md` (cross-reference, if it documents `/slots`)
- `scripts/verify_slots_observability.py` (new)
- `tests/test_verify_slots_observability.py` (new)
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_stale_reason_docs.py` (new: doc/code drift)

## Operator dependency

The live verification requires a proxy restart on the host. Use the
start-proxy skill (`/skill:start-proxy --restart`) — never kill the proxy
process directly. If a restart is not possible when this slice lands, record
the blocker on the parent item rather than marking the slice done.

## Plan: decomposition into 5 vertical slices

**Effort/risk (re-estimated with WBS):** Medium / High — 37.3 h recommended
range [29–51 h]. See the effort-and-risk report comment above.

### Key finding from code inspection (informs the split)

Two of the five change items in the description are **already merged on `dev`**
after the 2026-11-04 incident:

- change 1 (`?model=` on `/slots`) — `observability._resolve_slots_model_id` +
  `resolve_local_model_id` with a documented resolution order
  (LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW and related);
- change 2 (child-port discovery for autoloaded children) — the TTL'd,
  rotating child-port cache in `router_helpers` (LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF,
  LP-0MVWBXEAI008YZ7B).

What is **still absent** is the part that made the incident an 8-hour silent
freeze:

- the per-slot detail cache (`observability._last_slot_details_cache` /
  `_last_slot_details_at`) has **no age bound at all** — only the counts cache
  is bounded (`SLOT_COUNTS_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS`, 1 h);
- `slots_stale` is a bare boolean with no reason;
- `/health` reports nothing about the slot surface.

So slice 1 is a *regression fence* proving the merged work actually composes
end-to-end, and slices 2–4 add the missing bound + reason + health surface.

### Slices (test-first, dependency chain)

| # | Item | Type | Effort/Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Regression fence: router-mode `/slots` model param yields live detail (LP-0MW1VVGSI002O4HQ) | task (test-only) | S / Medium |
| 2 | Enumerated `slots_stale_reason` on local status payload (LP-0MW1VVIPG008896N) | feature | M / Medium |
| 3 | Bound the slot snapshot with `local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds` (LP-0MW1VVKPF001ZAV5) | feature | M / High |
| 4 | Surface slot staleness on `/health` (LP-0MW1VVMI1005XU0J) | feature | S / Medium |
| 5 | Docs, verify script and recorded live slot-observability evidence (LP-0MW1VVOJZ008YUPH) | docs | S / Low |

Dependency edges: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5.

### Vertical-slice check

Each slice cuts through all layers it needs: slice 1 is tests + reuse of the
fixture harness; slices 2–4 each ship code + its own tests + the docstring/doc
update for the field they add; slice 5 ships the operator doc, a deterministic
verification script with offline tests, and the recorded live evidence. No
slice is a single horizontal layer.

### Review discipline between slices

Before starting a slice, re-read its description and the *Out of scope* section
— in particular, the boundary with the siblings:

- LP-0MW1VDZIX0011D8M owns `available_slots` vs `slots[]` truth **when the data
  is fresh**; slice 3 only owns *the age bound*.
- LP-0MW1VDZTC00034S7 owns the llama-server lifecycle/log-path defects; slice 5
  reads that log for evidence but does not fix it.

### Plan decisions (assumptions, recorded for the implementer)

1. **`ready` on `/health` is deliberately not flipped** by slot staleness —
   `ready` gates request admission, and a stale slot *surface* does not make the
   proxy unable to serve (precedent: LP-0MVZT9L3N001XABB AC2). The non-OK
   signal is the new `slots_surface_status` field.
2. **The ceiling default is derived from the status poll cadence** in code, not
   a magic literal.
3. **Slice 1 must be green, not `xfail`** — if the composed assertion fails, the
   fix lands in slice 1.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required: intake had already completed with a
comprehensive problem statement, 5 change items and 8 acceptance criteria, and
the code inspection above resolved the only ambiguity (whether the `/slots`
model-param work was still outstanding). Decisions 1–3 are plan-time
assumptions, not answered questions, and are recorded above so they can be
challenged at implementation.

**OPEN QUESTION (for the producer, non-blocking):** should
`slots_surface_status: "stale"` also be consumed by `slot_sweep_preflight.py`
and machine-hygiene (i.e. should those tools refuse to act on a stale slot
surface)? Slice 4 adds the field but does not change any consumer; wiring them
is a separate, small follow-up if wanted.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-04T08:57Z — plan claimed `LP-0MW1VDWY0007EMH7` (`in_progress`, no
  assignee), inspected `proxy/proxy/{observability,handlers,router_helpers,residency}.py`
  and the existing slots test suite.
- 2026-11-04T08:57Z — created 5 child items (test-first) and wired the

- 2026-11-04T08:58Z — AC alignment pass: rewrote child ACs to restate the
  parent ACs verbatim where they are the same requirement; tree coverage review
  now reports 100 % (8/8 parent ACs covered), recommendation `proceed`.
- 2026-11-04T08:58Z — effort/risk estimator run with the WBS (Medium / High,
  37.3 h recommended); stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

## AC coverage map (parent AC → covering slice)

| Parent AC | Covered by |
|---|---|
| 1. router-mode fixture, detail not snapshot | slice 1 |
| 2. `slots_snapshot_age_seconds` bounded | slice 3 |
| 3. enumerated `slots_stale` reason, all values covered | slice 2 |
| 4. stale slot surface in `/health` (non-OK) | slice 4 |
